title: Shard-aware tiered deadlines and hybrid fallback routing for reranking endpoint
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce P95/P99 tail latency for reranking requests while preserving top-k quality and supporting multi-region failover. We will implement shard-aware tiered deadlines (per-shard soft deadlines + global hard deadline), a hybrid fanout fallback policy (local cached rerank, cold-region fallback, and degraded-scoring mode), and a circuit breaker layer that trips per-region and per-shard to avoid cascading latency during load spikes.

Background: Several incidents in Q4 showed long tail latency when embeddings/rerank fanout hit noisy GPU nodes or slow storage-backed shard lookups. Current single global timeout causes sloppy retries and amplifies load. Previous tickets (see dependencies) introduced admission control and local caching, but we still see region-induced hotspots.

Scope:
- Implement per-shard soft time budgets derived from historic shard latency quantiles and dynamic load.
- Enforce a global hard deadline for end-to-end rerank responses.
- Add a regional circuit breaker that tracks SLA breaches and error budgets and opens to route to cached or degraded models.
- Add degraded-scoring fallback that returns a lightweight approximate rerank (embedding-only score + simple recency signal) when primary reranker times out.
- Expose config knobs in control plane: quantile (Q90/Q95/Q99), shard weight caps, breaker thresholds, and fallback strategy order.

Success criteria (metrics to monitor):
- Reduce P99 latency by >= 30% under 95th-percentile load scenarios in staging.
- Maintain top-3 rerank precision@3 within 3% of baseline for traffic-sampled prompts when fallback triggers.
- Avoid increased error rates > 0.5% due to fallbacks.
- No customer-facing incidents after rollout for 30 days.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Fallback scorers degrade relevance. Mitigation: ship guarded rollout with A/B sampling and eval harness comparing baseline vs degraded scorer on production prompt corpus.
- Risk: Mis-tuned breakers cause over-eviction. Mitigation: conservative defaults, canary in single region, adaptive cooldown.
- Risk: Performance regression from added bookkeeping. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and runtime-level counters; use lightweight probabilistic bookkeeping where possible.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement feature flags + control plane config (internal only).
2) Canary in staging with 1% of traffic and observability dashboards.
3) Canary in primary region 5% traffic for 48h.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% while monitoring quality regressions and latency.
5) Full rollout after 7 days with kill-switch.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the serving-layer orchestration and runtime hooks. Algorithmic improvements to the reranker scoring model should be tracked in a follow-up evaluation ticket.
comments: 2025-02-05 - Arjun Patel: Groomed with PM + Runtime. Agreed on shard-aware deadlines to avoid hairy retry storms. Decided to prioritize hybrid fallback over full synchronous fanout reduction to preserve quality when possible.

2025-02-07 - Samira Chen: Initial spike completed. Prototype calculates per-shard 95th quantile using sliding 1h window. Observed heavy variance on GPU-backed shard 7. Need storage-layer histograms for cold starts.

2025-02-10 - Design review (pm): Maria Gonzalez: UX for fallback signals in Console - add per-route 'degraded' badge and histogram of fallback rate. Action: ENG to add metrics emission (rerank.fallback_rate, rerank.breaker_open_count).
2025-02-12 - Infra feedback: K8s pod eviction on high mem pressure may skew shard latency. Action: add node-label-aware routing to avoid recently-evicted nodes. Raised ENG-88701 as follow-up.
2025-02-14 - Samira Chen: Implemented regional breaker prototype. Config: open when error_rate > 2% for 1m and p99 latency > 1200ms. Added exponential backoff for half-open trials.

2025-02-17 - QA: Ran A/B with degraded scorer at 2% traffic. Precision@3 drop measured: 1.8%. Feedback: acceptable, but certain query types (legal text) saw larger drops. Decided to add query-class routing to avoid fallback for high-sensitivity customers.
2025-02-19 - Pull request: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-runtime/pull/612 - Adds tiered-deadline scheduler, breaker hooks, and fallback scorer integration. Pending perf review.

2025-02-20 - Observability: Dashboard draft: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rerank/tiered-deadlines - includes per-shard latency heatmap, breaker events, fallback hits by region. Alert: rerank.breaker_open_count > 0 for >5m triggers PagerDuty.
2025-02-21 - Samira Chen: Perf microbenchmarks show scheduler overhead ~0.6ms/request median. Approved to proceed to staging canary next week.
